name: Thoracic Discogenic Pain
definition: Axial thoracic pain suspected to arise from an intervertebral disc after exclusion of visceral, fracture, inflammatory and neural-compressive causes.

typical: Pain with sustained posture or movement

investigations.principle: MRI is reserved for persistent symptoms or red flags; disc degeneration alone does not prove pain causation.
investigations.MRI: Use MRI when neural, soft-tissue, marrow, infection, tumor or occult-injury assessment requires it.
investigations.radiographs: Use radiographs and/or CT according to the condition-specific diagnostic pathway.

amber: Avoid attributing thoracic pain to disc degeneration without excluding serious non-spinal causes.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Prishtha-shoola phenotype may be documented only in parallel.

patientEducation.summary: Axial thoracic pain suspected to arise from an intervertebral disc after exclusion of visceral, fracture, inflammatory and neural-compressive causes.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for acute/progressive neurological deficit, severe vascular symptoms, major trauma, suspected infection, pathological fracture, neurovascular compromise or other listed red flags.
